title: Smooth subgroups with spanning tangent spaces generate a connected group
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Group schemes and homomorphisms are as in [def-sc-group-scheme], closed subgroup schemes as in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], smoothness as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], connectedness as in [def-weil-connected-scheme], and finite type as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $G$ be a smooth connected affine $F$-group scheme of finite type. Let $I$ be a finite set, possibly empty, and for $i\in I$ let $H_i\hookrightarrow G$ be smooth connected closed subgroup schemes. For a group scheme $J$, write $\operatorname{Lie}(J)=T_eJ=(\mathfrak m_e/\mathfrak m_e^2)^\vee$ for its tangent space at its identity; a homomorphism induces its differential there. Suppose that the images of the linear maps $\operatorname{Lie}(H_i)\to\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ together span $\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ as an $F$-vector space. Then for every closed subgroup scheme $K\subseteq G$ through which all the inclusions $H_i\hookrightarrow G$ factor, one has $K=G$. No smoothness or connectedness is assumed for $K$, and the assertion includes the empty family.

source.place: Corollary 10.17 and its proof, printed p.191; linear-span specialization of its Lie-generation hypothesis.

proof.text: Fix a closed subgroup $K\subseteq G$ containing all the $H_i$. Write $G=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $K=\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ using [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The quotient is generated by the images of any finite set of $F$-algebra generators of $A$, so $K$ is affine of finite type. Apply [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component] to $K$: its identity component $K^0$ is open and closed and $L=(K^0)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a smooth connected integral group scheme of finite type, with the same underlying space as $K^0$. The inclusion $L\to G$ is closed: on the open-and-closed pieces $K^0$ and its complement in $K$, its ideal is respectively the nilradical and the unit ideal; composing with $K\to G$ composes the surjections on structure sheaves. Thus $L$ is an affine closed subgroup of $G$.

source.place: Corollary 10.17 and Proposition 10.15, printed pp.190–191; reduced-identity-component variant using Stacks 0B7R and 047R.

proof.text: For each $i$, let $f_i:H_i\to K$ be the assumed factorization. The inverse image of $K^0$ is open and closed in $H_i$ and contains its identity; its complement is empty by connectedness [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Restricting the target sheaf to this open subset gives a morphism $H_i\to K^0$ by [def-weil-open-immersion]. $H_i$ is reduced: by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] it is covered by affine opens $V$ with $F\to\mathcal O(V)$ a smooth ring map, each $\mathcal O(V)$ is reduced by [lem-sfb-smooth-algebra-over-reduced-ring] since $F$ is, and then its local rings, localizations of reduced rings, are reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] to factor it through $L=(K^0)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Denote the factor by $a_i:H_i\to L$ and the inclusion by $j:L\hookrightarrow G$. These factors are homomorphisms: after inclusion in $G$, their multiplication, identity and inverse identities are those of $H_i\to G$, and an inclusion of closed subschemes is injective on morphisms, as is seen from its surjections on structure sheaves. Hence $H_i\to G=j\circ a_i$ as homomorphisms.

source.place: Corollary 10.17 and Proposition 10.15, printed pp.190–191; reduced-identity-component variant using Stacks 0B7R and 047R.

proof.text: Put $V=\operatorname{im}(\mathrm dj)\subseteq\operatorname{Lie}(G)$. The tangent-map definition in [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space] makes composition of differentials composition of maps (both send a dual-number point $\theta$ to $j\circ a_i\circ\theta$). Consequently every image $\operatorname{im}(\operatorname{Lie}(H_i)\to\operatorname{Lie}(G))$ is contained in $V$, and the spanning hypothesis implies $V=\operatorname{Lie}(G)$. Also $\mathrm dj$ is injective: the closed immersion gives a surjection $\mathcal O_{G,e}\to\mathcal O_{L,e}$ and hence a surjection of maximal-ideal quotients $\mathfrak m_{G,e}/\mathfrak m_{G,e}^2\to\mathfrak m_{L,e}/\mathfrak m_{L,e}^2$. By [lem-sc-rational-tangent-cotangent-duality], its dual is $\mathrm dj$; a functional whose pullback along a surjection is zero is zero. Thus $\mathrm dj$ is a linear isomorphism. This argument also applies to $I=\varnothing$: its span is zero, so the hypothesis says $\operatorname{Lie}(G)=0$.

source.place: Corollary 10.17 and Proposition 10.15, printed pp.190–191; reduced-identity-component variant using Stacks 0B7R and 047R.

proof.text: Apply [lem-ag-smooth-lie-local-dimension] to the smooth groups $L$ and $G$, and [lem-ag-group-identity-local-dimension] to these finite-type groups. Their statements give $\dim L=\dim_F\operatorname{Lie}(L)$ and $\dim G=\dim_F\operatorname{Lie}(G)$. The isomorphism in the preceding step therefore gives $\dim L=\dim G$. Here Lie means the tangent space at the rational identity as explicitly defined in the item; neither dimension statement assumes characteristic zero.

source.place: Corollary 10.17 and Proposition 10.15, printed pp.190–191; reduced-identity-component variant using Stacks 0B7R and 047R.

proof.text: The smooth scheme $G=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is reduced: $F\to A$ is a smooth ring map by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], so $A$ is reduced by [lem-sfb-smooth-algebra-over-reduced-ring]. Because $G$ is connected, $G^0=G$. Applying [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component] to $G$ shows that $(G^0)_{\mathrm{red}}=G$ is integral, in particular irreducible. Now [lem-wf-affine-dimension-drop] applies to the irreducible reduced affine finite-type $F$-scheme $G$. If the closed subset $|L|$ were proper, it would give $\dim L\leq\dim G-1$, contradicting the dimension equality. Thus $|L|=|G|$.

source.place: Corollary 10.17 and Proposition 10.15, printed pp.190–191; reduced-identity-component variant using Stacks 0B7R and 047R.

proof.text: Since $G$ is reduced and $|L|=|G|$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] with $Y=X=G$, $Z=L$ and $f=\operatorname{id}_G$. It gives a factorization $G\to L\to G$ of the identity, so $L=G$ as closed subschemes (on affine rings the ideal of $L$ maps to zero under the identity, hence is zero). Finally $L\subseteq K\subseteq G$ implies $K=G$: their defining ideals satisfy $0=I_L\supseteq I_K\supseteq0$. We never assumed that $K$ was smooth, reduced or connected.

source.place: Corollary 10.17 and Proposition 10.15, printed pp.190–191; reduced-identity-component variant using Stacks 0B7R and 047R.
